chapter: Steamer Capitol and New Orleans bands
title: The Sunny South Syncopators
summary: He lists the members of the Sunny South Syncopators, including Leo Dejean, Joe Phillips and Eddie Pearson.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Peerron. No, I met his widow. I knew Clarence Williams, his partner in the music business. Yes. I went down there to meet him one year and he died a few months before and I talked to his widow that summer.
Well, there was another group that had a very good band at that particular time and it was called the Sonny South Syncopators.
Well, who was in that? You never heard about that?

I don't think so. Well a cousin of mine was playing for his first trumpet, Leo Dejon, Harold Dejon's brother. He's got a brother out there in the west coast now. And there was another fellow by the name of Joe Phillips, he played trumpet. He plays in the bass. Yeah, incidentally he was one of Chalini's pupils, one of Chalini's dark pupils. And there was another fellow by the name of Sidney Montague, he played drums.
I've heard of him, I don't know him.
Eddie Pearson, I know you know Eddie Pearson.
Oh yeah, sure. Yeah, trombone. That's right.

He was one of the main stems in the group. Eddie Pearson and let's see, there was another guy who played a wonderful clarinet. His name was Elliot. What was Elliot's last name? Well I don't think he's in New Orleans now. I think he left New Orleans a good while ago.
